title: Take-up Rate and Affordability of After-school Student Care Centres
what_it_is: Take-up Rate and Affordability of After-school Student Care Centres

sections.label: Student care centre enrolment and fees
sections.summary: School-based student care enrolment rose from 3,000 in 2012 to 21,000, with SCCs in all primary schools by end 2020 and fee assistance for needy families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Their enrolment has increased from 3,000 in 2012 to 21,000 today, or 9% of all primary school students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Where there is demand for school-based student care services, schools will work closely with the service providers to expand their capacity at a pace that does not compromise quality.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: MOE is on track to have SCCs in all our primary schools by end 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Currently, there are 261 community-based SCCs registered with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), with a total enrolment of about 11,000 students, and with some spare capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: To ensure affordability for children from lower-income families, the ComCare Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA) scheme provides needy families with assistance to offset their monthly SCC fees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: With the assistance, eligible students can pay as little as $5 per month.

sections.label: Training programme for SCC staff
sections.summary: MOE, MSF and Workforce Singapore introduced a 40-hour training programme for new and untrained SCC staff, run by Ngee Ann Polytechnic since 2015, training about 622 staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: To uplift the quality of SCC staff, MOE, MSF and Workforce Development Agency ‒ now, Workforce Singapore ‒ have introduced a 40-hour training programme for new and untrained SCC staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: This course is currently undertaken by Ngee Ann Polytechnic and was launched in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: So far, it has trained about 622 staff to date.
